284	#### Step 6b — Run configure
285	
286	After adding the node with `uip maestro flow node add`, configure it with the resolved connection and field values.
287	
288	**Concrete activity** (Jira `curated_create_issue` — object encoded in node type):
289	
290	```bash
291	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> \
292	  --detail '{"connectionId": "<id>", "folderKey": "<key>", "method": "POST", "endpoint": "/issues", "bodyParameters": {"fields.project.key": "ENGCE", "fields.issuetype.id": "10004"}}' \
293	  --output json
294	```
295	
296	**Generic activity, list** (Salesforce `list-records` against Opportunity — object selected at configure time, no per-record input):
297	
298	```bash
299	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> \
300	  --detail '{"connectionId": "<id>", "folderKey": "<key>", "method": "GET", "endpoint": "/Opportunity", "objectName": "Opportunity"}' \
301	  --output json
302	```
303	
304	**Generic activity, retrieve-by-id** (Salesforce `get-record` against Account — object plus a path parameter for the record ID):
305	
306	```bash
307	uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> \
308	  --detail '{"connectionId": "<id>", "folderKey": "<key>", "method": "GETBYID", "endpoint": "/Account/{accountId}", "objectName": "Account", "pathParameters": {"accountId": "001KY000007uI02YAE"}}' \
309	  --output json
310	```
311	
312	Path-parameterized GETs are a distinct shape from list/query: `endpoint` carries `{<placeholder>}` tokens and `pathParameters` supplies the values. Resolve the ID via `is resources run list <connector-key> <objectName>` (Step 4) — never paste IDs across connections (see [reference-resolution.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/reference-resolution.md#reference-ids-are-connection-scoped-critical)).
313	
314	The `objectName` field is required for generic nodes (see "Generic vs Concrete Activities" above). The CLI fails fast with a runnable hint when it's missing on a generic node. For concrete nodes the field is ignored if supplied.
315	
316	**Source of truth for `method` and `endpoint`** — pick either (both read the same upstream IS metadata):
317	
318	- `registry get` (Step 2) → `connectorMethodInfo.method` and `connectorMethodInfo.path` — populated for **concrete** activities only.
319	- `is resources describe <connector-key> <objectName> --operation <Op>` (Step 3) → `availableOperations[].method` and `availableOperations[].path` — works for both, and is the only source for **generic** activities.
320	
321	> **Method label — pass the IS describe value verbatim.** `is resources describe` sometimes returns synthesized IS-side labels (notably `"GETBYID"` for path-parameterized retrieve operations). The CLI accepts both standard HTTP verbs (`GET`, `POST`, …) and IS-side labels (`GETBYID`) — copy `operation.method` from `is resources describe` as-is and the CLI normalizes to the underlying HTTP verb internally. Don't translate by hand.
322	
323	> **`flow validate` cross-checks `method` against the activity's `operation`.** If the value you pass disagrees with the operation baked into the node by `node add` (e.g. `method: "POST"` on a Retrieve activity), validate fails with `HTTP method "<X>" does not match operation "<Y>". Expected "<Z>"`. This catches stale copy-paste — fix by re-reading `operation.method` from `is resources describe` against the right `--operation`.
324	
325	Body field names in `bodyParameters` come from `inputDefinition.fields[].name` (`registry get`, concrete only) or `requestFields[].name` (`is resources describe`, both).
326	
327	> **Array fields — `[*]` indicates an array.** `[*]` in `requestFields[].name` (or `inputDefinition.fields[].name`) marks the field as an array; `dataType` identifies the element type. **Supported only when `[*]` is the name suffix.** Any name containing `[*].` (path segments after the `[*]`, e.g. `addresses[*].zipCode`, `contacts[*].emails[*]`) is not authorable — the canvas UI does not emit these shapes. The rule below covers `bodyParameters`, `queryParameters`, and `pathParameters`.
328	>
329	> | `requestFields[].name` | `dataType` | Authoring shape in `inputs.detail` |
330	> |---|---|---|
331	> | `fields.labels[*]` | `string` | `"fields.labels": "=js:(['shield', 'p0'])"` |
332	> | `fields.components_arrayRemap_name[*]` | `string` | `"fields.components_arrayRemap_name": "=js:(['IS Runtime'])"` |
333	> | `users[*]` | `string` | `"users": "=js:(['U123ABC', 'U456DEF'])"` |
334	>
335	> **Strip `[*]` from the key; pass a `=js:` expression returning the array.**  The runtime rejects any key containing the literal `[*]` substring as unknown (regardless of value shape), so pass the stripped form in your `node configure --detail` payload. **A literal JSON array (`"users": ["U123ABC", "U456DEF"]`) passes `node configure` and `flow validate` but does not bind — the field round-trips empty.** **Distinct from `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues`**, where `[*]` is encoded as `_array` — see Step 6c.
336	>
337	> **Expression values.** The serializer is purely structural (dot-expansion only; no expression evaluation, no type coercion). Choose the authoring shape based on what the expression returns at runtime:
338	>
339	> | Expression resolves to | Authoring shape | Example |
340	> |---|---|---|
341	> | The whole array | `"<field>": "=<expr>"` | `"fields.labels": "=js:$vars.allTags"` |
342	> | A single element to wrap | `"<field>": "=js:([<expr>])"` | `"fields.labels": "=js:([$vars.priorityTag])"` |
343	
344	> **Connector output shape — derive it from `connectorMethodInfo`, never from vendor-API intuition.**
345	>
346	> | `connectorMethodInfo.operation` | `output` at runtime | Loop / binding shape |
347	> |---|---|---|
348	> | `list` | bare **array**; `outputResponseDefinition.fields` describes one element | `"collection": "=js:$vars.<node>.output"` |
349	> | anything else (`retrieve`, `create`, `update`, …) | single **object** matching those fields | `=js:$vars.<node>.output.<field>` |
350	>
351	> Ignore `outputDefinition.output.type` — it says `"object"` even for `list` operations, where the actual output type is an array.
352	
353	The command populates `inputs.detail` and creates workflow-level `bindings` entries. Use **resolved IDs** from Step 4, not display names. For FilterBuilder params, see Step 6a.
354	
355	When inspecting the resulting `.flow`, note that the folder field is named `connectionFolderKey` in `inputs.detail`. The CLI `--detail` input accepts `folderKey` for convenience, then serializes the `.flow` field expected by validation. Do not hand-edit this field — `inputs.detail` is CLI-owned (see [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)); re-run `node configure` to change it.
356	
357	> **Do not use `filterExpression`** — that field is the trigger / JMESPath path. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md#filter-trees).
358	
359	> **Shell quoting tip:** For complex `--detail` JSON, write it to a temp file: `uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> --detail "$(cat /tmp/detail.json)" --output json`

361	#### Step 6c — Populate custom fields (api-type ObjectActions)
362	
363	A connector activity has a **parent-field-driven schema** when its valid input fields are not fixed in static metadata but are computed at design time by running an api-type ObjectAction against the IS Element Service. Examples: Jira's `Create Issue` schema depends on the project + issue type; Snowflake's `executeQuery` response columns depend on the SQL string; Dataservice V3's entity field set depends on `tenantEntityName`. The activity persists the parent-field values in `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails` so the runtime can replay the schema-fetch ObjectAction on each invocation. The CLI passes this through verbatim.
364	
365	**How DAP determines support — check both metadata locations.** An api-type action may live at either:
366	
367	- Top-level `objectActions[]` with PascalCase `ActionType: "Api"` (older shape, e.g. Jira `GenerateSchema`)
368	- `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` with lowercase `actionType: "api"` (newer shape, e.g. Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant`)
369	
370	The dispatcher matches `ObjectActionType.Api === 'api'` (case-sensitive lowercase string) — both shapes go through the same `_processCustomFieldsRequestAction` code path with no per-connector branching. Always inspect both locations from `registry get` output before deciding the connector has none.
371	
372	The matching action is then selected by one of two rule sources:
373	
374	- **`source: field`** — the action's `rules[].refFieldName` are satisfied by user-supplied `-f, --field` values (typically SQL-style query connectors where the query string is the parent field).
375	- **`source: method`** — the action is declared at the operation level and matched against the operation's HTTP method (typically CRUD activities).
376	
377	**Examples of supported activities.** The list below is illustrative, not exhaustive — DAP's actual support set evolves with connector metadata. Always confirm by inspecting `objectActions[]` / `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` from `registry get` for the specific (connector, object, activity) you're configuring.
378	
379	| Connector key | Object | Activity / Action | HTTP | Source |
380	|---|---|---|---|---|
381	| `uipath-microsoft-azureapplicationinsights` | `executeQuery` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
382	| `uipath-salesforce-sfdc` | `curated_soqlQuery` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
383	| `uipath-workday-workdayrest` | `wql` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
384	| `uipath-oracle-netsuite` | `executeSuiteQL` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
385	| `uipath-snowflake-snowflake` | `executeQuery` | `generateSchema` | — | field |
386	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `curated_create_issue` | Create Issue | POST | method |
387	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `curated_edit_issue` | Update Issue | PUT | method |
388	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `curated_get_issue` | Get Issue | GETBYID | method |
389	| `uipath-uipath-dataservice` | `CreateEntityRecordCurated` | Create Entity Record | POST | method |
390	| `uipath-uipath-dataservice` | `QueryEntityRecordsCurated` | Query Entity Records | POST | method |

396	If neither metadata location contains an `actionType: "api"` / `ActionType: "Api"` entry for the activity you're configuring, it has no parent-field-driven schema — omit `customFieldsRequestDetails` (CLI emits `null`).
397	
398	Each api-type entry has `name` (the `ObjectActionName`) and `apiConfiguration.{url,body}` with `{token}` placeholders — those tokens name the parent fields whose values must be in `parameterValues`.
399	
400	**Script:** `python3 scripts/encode_parameter_values.py --field '<parentField>=<value>' [--field ...] [--object-action-name <ObjectActionName>] [--bucket bodyParameters|queryParameters|pathParameters]` emits `parameterValues` as encoded tuples plus the raw-keyed `runtimeParameters` copy, so both halves of the contract go into `--detail`. `--encode-only '<token>'` prints one encoded key. Which parent fields the activity needs still comes from the metadata you read above.
401	
402	**Token encoding rule.** Tokens are encoded via `NamingHelper.getValidIdentifier` (the IS-side identifier sanitizer) before being used as `parameterValues` keys, so they match design-property names at lookup time. Substitutions (applied longest-first):
403	
404	| Match in token | Encoded as |
405	|---|---|
406	| `:::` | `_sub_` |
407	| `[*]` | `_array` |
408	| `::` | `_sub_` |
409	| `.` | `_sub_` |
410	
411	Examples: `fields.project.key` → `fields_sub_project_sub_key`; `items[*]` → `items_array`; `tenantEntityName` → `tenantEntityName` (unchanged). When in doubt, inspect a working `.flow` for the encoded form.
412	
413	> **`customFieldsRequestDetails` is COMPLEMENTARY to `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters`, not a substitute.** Same parent-field values must appear in BOTH places, with different keys:
414	>
415	> | Location | Purpose | Key shape |
416	> |---|---|---|
417	> | `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` | Runtime input — what the connector actually sends to its API | **Raw** field names (e.g. `fields.project.key`, `tenantEntityName`) |
418	> | `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues` | Design-time replay cache — drives the parent-field-driven schema fetch when the activity is re-opened or re-validated | **Encoded** keys (e.g. `fields_sub_project_sub_key`, `tenantEntityName`) |
419	>
420	> Concrete (Jira Create Issue): `bodyParameters.fields.project.key = "ENGCE"` AND `parameterValues = [["fields_sub_project_sub_key", "ENGCE"]]`. Concrete (Dataservice V3): `queryParameters.tenantEntityName = ""my-entity""` AND `parameterValues = [["tenantEntityName", ""my-entity""]]`. Dropping the runtime-input copy on the assumption that the cache covers it leaves the runtime with no field value to bind — manifests as `DAP-DT-_2003 refField with name <X> not found` at activity load.
421	
422	**Shape (verified against Solution 386 — Jira Create Issue):**
423	
424	```json
425	"customFieldsRequestDetails": {
426	  "objectActionName": "GenerateSchema",
427	  "parameterValues": [
428	    ["fields_sub_project_sub_key", "ENGCE"],
429	    ["fields_sub_issuetype_sub_id", "3"]
430	  ]
431	}
432	```
433	
434	Rules:
435	
436	- camelCase keys (`objectActionName`, `parameterValues`). PascalCase rejected at validate time.
437	- `parameterValues` is an **array of `[key, value]` tuples** — never an object map. The IS-side serializer emits a `Map<string,string|null>` via `Array.from(entries())`; the CLI rejects object-map form.
438	- Tuple value is `string` or `null`. Use `null` for tokens the user has not yet set.
439	- The CLI does NOT validate ObjectAction existence or token coverage at configure time. **Always run Step 3a first** with the planned parent-field combination — if it errors with `No api-type ObjectAction matched for fields [...]`, the cache you're about to write is wrong (adjust tokens or action name); if it succeeds, the response confirms the action and tokens are real, and you author `customFieldsRequestDetails` from that result, not from memory or doc examples. Read `apiConfiguration.url` / `body` from the matched action (top-level `objectActions[]` OR `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]`) to enumerate required tokens.
440	
441	**CLI invocation — pass BOTH halves.** The runtime input bucket (`bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters`) AND the design-time cache (`customFieldsRequestDetails`) must both appear in the same `--detail`. Omitting the runtime bucket is the most common mistake — the cache alone does not feed the connector at runtime.

540	uip is connectors list --output json
541	```
542	
543	Run `uip is connections --help` or `uip is resources --help` for all options.
544	
545	---
546	
547	## Bindings — top-level `.flow` `bindings[]`
548	
549	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. Bindings are authored in the flow's **top-level `bindings[]` array** (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`). At `flow debug` / `flow pack` time the CLI regenerates `content/bindings_v2.json` from these entries.
550	
551	> **Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly.** Any manual edits are overwritten on the next debug/pack. All authoring flows through the `.flow` file's top-level `bindings[]`.
552	
553	### How connector nodes reference bindings
554	
555	The connector node's **definition** (the manifest copied from `uip maestro flow registry get` into `definitions[]`) carries a `model.context[]` template like this. **Leave the definition exactly as the registry returns it** — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the definition, and do NOT author `model.context[]` on the instance:
556	
557	```json
558	"context": [
559	  { "name": "connectorKey", "type": "string", "value": "uipath-atlassian-jira" },
560	  { "name": "connection", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.uipath-atlassian-jira connection>" },
561	  { "name": "folderKey", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.FolderKey>" }
562	]
563	```
564	
565	At BPMN emit time, the runtime rewrites each `<bindings.{name}>` placeholder to `=bindings.{id}` by finding a top-level `bindings[]` entry whose `name` matches the placeholder. For connectors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is typically unset, so matching is **name-only** within the `resource: "Connection"` candidate set.
566	
567	> **Matching differs from resource nodes.** For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is set to `<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>`, so placeholder matching is scoped by `(name, resourceKey)`. For connector nodes, `resourceKey` on the definition is typically unset, so matching is name-only — the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder must be unique per connector in the flow. Don't confuse the two patterns.
568	
569	### Top-level `bindings[]` shape (CLI-emitted; reference only)
570	
571	`uip maestro flow node configure` populates these entries — you do not author them by hand. The schema below is the shape the CLI emits, for **inspection** when debugging a flow's binding state and as the planned shape for the **No-Live-Tenant** flow's sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` (see § No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration above). Per the [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) rules, `bindings[]` is part of the CLI-owned envelope for connector / connector-trigger / managed HTTP nodes.
572	
573	For every unique connection used in the flow, `node configure` appends **two entries** to top-level `bindings[]`:
574	
575	```json
576	"bindings": [
577	  {
578	    "id": "<CONN_BINDING_ID>",
579	    "name": "<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection",
580	    "type": "string",
581	    "resource": "Connection",
582	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
583	    "default": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
584	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
585	  },
586	  {
587	    "id": "<FOLDER_BINDING_ID>",
588	    "name": "FolderKey",
589	    "type": "string",
590	    "resource": "Connection",
591	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
592	    "default": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
593	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
594	  }
595	]
596	```
597	
598	| Field | Value |
599	|-------|-------|
600	| `id` | Unique string within the file. Descriptive (e.g. `bJiraConn`) or short random (e.g. `bKEFLMRB2`). |
601	| `name` (connection binding) | The IS connection name (e.g. `"chandu.lella@uipath.com #3"`). `uip maestro flow node configure` fetches this from IS automatically — this is the supported path. The placeholder form `"<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection"` appears in the table for reference only (e.g. when inspecting a flow whose bindings have not yet been configured); it must match the definition's `model.context[].connection` placeholder (without the `<bindings.` prefix and `>` suffix). |
602	| `name` (folder binding) | Literal `"FolderKey"` — matches `<bindings.FolderKey>`. |
603	| `type` | Always `"string"`. |
604	| `resource` | Always `"Connection"` — capital C, case-sensitive. |
605	| `resourceKey` | The connection UUID from `uip is connections list`. **Same UUID on both bindings.** |
606	| `default` | Connection binding → connection UUID. Folder binding → folder key. |
607	| `propertyAttribute` | `"ConnectionId"` or `"FolderKey"` — case matters. |
608	
609	The connector node instance carries no `model` block and no binding/context data. `uip maestro flow node configure` populates only `inputs.detail` on the instance and writes the two top-level `bindings[]` entries — claiming the empty `ConnectionId` stub that `node add` hoisted (matched by name) and adding the `FolderKey` row. The connection UUID is held on the binding entry (`resourceKey`), not on the node.
610	
611	> **An empty-keyed Connection binding is a defect, not a cosmetic nit.** A `bindings[]` row with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"`, and `resourceKey: ""` faults Studio Web at runtime with `Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'Connection')`. `node add` hoists exactly one such stub (`name: "<connector-key> connection"`); `node configure` **claims it in place** (matching by that name), so a fully configured connector leaves no empty row — do not expect a "duplicate" empty pair, and never hand-edit `bindings[]` to remove one (it is CLI-owned). The only legitimate empty stub is the No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration case above, where the node is deliberately left unconfigured and the flow is known not to pass `flow validate` yet. An empty stub that survives a real `node configure` — or lingers after a connector node is removed — is a CLI bug to report, not something to paper over by hand.
612	
613	**Share bindings across nodes using the same connection.** If two connector nodes share the same `<CONNECTION_UUID>`, reuse the same two binding entries — do not add duplicates. Matching is by `name` only (the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder is unique per connector), so any node whose definition resolves against `<bindings.<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection>` picks up the shared binding pair.
614	
615	### Single-connector example (Jira)
616	
617	```json
618	"bindings": [
619	  {
620	    "id": "bJiraConn",
621	    "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",
622	    "type": "string",
623	    "resource": "Connection",
624	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
625	    "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
626	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
627	  },
628	  {
629	    "id": "bJiraFolder",
630	    "name": "FolderKey",
631	    "type": "string",
632	    "resource": "Connection",
633	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
634	    "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
635	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
636	  }
637	]
638	```
639	
640	### Multi-connector example (Jira + Slack)
641	
642	Two unique connections → four entries in `bindings[]` (two per connection):
643	
644	```json
645	"bindings": [
646	  { "id": "bJiraConn",   "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",   "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
647	  { "id": "bJiraFolder", "name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "folder-uuid-for-jira",                "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" },
648	  { "id": "bSlackConn",  "name": "uipath-salesforce-slack connection", "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
649	  { "id": "bSlackFolder","name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "folder-uuid-for-slack",               "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" }
650	]
651	```
652	
653	Both `FolderKey` entries share the same `name` but have distinct `resourceKey`s — that's how the runtime keeps them separate.
654	
655	### Generated `bindings_v2.json` (reference only — do not edit)
656	
657	At debug/pack time, the CLI derives `content/bindings_v2.json` from the top-level `bindings[]` above. One `Connection` resource per unique `resourceKey`; the `FolderKey` bindings are absorbed as metadata (they do not produce standalone resource entries). The generated output looks like:
658	
659	```json
660	{
661	  "version": "2.0",
662	  "resources": [
663	    {
664	      "resource": "Connection",
665	      "key": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
666	      "id": "Connection7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
667	      "value": {
668	        "ConnectionId": {
669	          "defaultValue": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
670	          "isExpression": false,
671	          "displayName": "my-jira-connection"
672	        }
673	      },
674	      "metadata": {
675	        "ActivityName": "Create Issue",
676	        "BindingsVersion": "2.2",
677	        "DisplayLabel": "my-jira-connection",
678	        "UseConnectionService": "true",
679	        "Connector": "uipath-atlassian-jira"
680	      }
681	    }
682	  ]
683	}
684	```
685	
686	- `id` is always `"Connection" + <resourceKey>` (concatenated, no separator) — generated, not authored.
687	- `metadata.Connector` is derived from the definition's `model.context[].connectorKey`.
688	- `metadata.ActivityName` comes from the matched node's `display.label`.
689	
690	### Other binding resource types (triggers, queues, scheduled)
691	
692	For connector-trigger flows, the same pattern applies — top-level `bindings[]` entries with additional metadata; the CLI derives `EventTrigger` and `Property` resources for `bindings_v2.json`. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md) for the trigger-specific shape.
693	
694	| Generated `bindings_v2.json` resource | Authored via | Key source fields |
695	|---------------------------------------|--------------|-------------------|
696	| `Connection` | Top-level `bindings[]` with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"` | Covered above |
697	| `EventTrigger` | Top-level `bindings[]` + the trigger node itself | See connector-trigger plugin |
698	| `Property` | Trigger node's `model.inputs.filterFields` | See connector-trigger plugin |
699	| `Queue` / `TimeTrigger` | Specific trigger types | See relevant trigger plugin |
700	
701	> **Never hardcode connection IDs.** Always fetch them from IS at authoring time. Connection IDs are tenant-specific and change across environments.
702	
703	---
704	
705	## Debug
706	
707	### Common Errors
708	
709	| Error | Cause | Fix |
710	| --- | --- | --- |
711	| No connection found | Connection not bound — top-level `bindings[]` missing or `resourceKey` doesn't match the node | Run Step 1 above to bind a connection; verify both entries (`ConnectionId` + `FolderKey`) are in the top-level `bindings[]` |
712	| Connection ping failed | Connection expired or misconfigured | Re-authenticate the connection in the IS portal |
713	| Missing `inputs.detail` | Node added but not configured | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` with the detail JSON (Step 6) |
714	| Reference field has display name instead of ID | `uip is resources run list` was skipped | Resolve the reference field to get the actual ID (Step 4) |
715	| Node faults at runtime with "resource not found" or similar after a clean build and validate | Reference field uses an ID scoped to a **different** connection (common when copying from a prior flow in the same session — e.g., a Slack channel ID from workspace A pasted into a node bound to workspace B's connection) | Re-run `uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID>`, extract the fresh ID, update `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` in `--detail`, re-run `node configure`, re-debug. See Step 4 and the top-level Anti-Pattern on reference-ID reuse in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md). |
716	| Required field missing at runtime | Required input field not provided | Check metadataFile for all `required: true` fields in both `requestFields` and `parameters` |
717	| `$vars` expression unresolvable | Node outputs block missing or node not connected | Verify the node has edges and upstream outputs are correctly referenced |
718	| `connectorMethodInfo` missing method/path | Used `registry get` without `--connection-id` | Re-run with `--connection-id` for enriched metadata (Step 2) |
719	| `bindings_v2.json` malformed or stale | It was hand-edited (the CLI overwrites edits on next debug/pack), or top-level `bindings[]` was mutated by hand | Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly. Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` on the affected connector node(s) so the CLI re-emits top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from those at the next debug/pack. Compare the emitted shape against the CLI-emitted reference in § Top-level `bindings[]` shape. |
720	| Connector key not found | Wrong key name | Run `uip is connectors list --output json` — keys are often prefixed with `uipath-` |
721	| FilterBuilder UI shows `undefined` when activity is reopened in Studio Web; flow runs at debug | A raw `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` string was passed instead of a structured filter tree, so `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>` is empty. The runtime side works but Studio Web has no tree to render. | Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` with `--detail '{"filter": {...tree...}}'` — the CLI populates both halves. See Step 6a above and [uipath-platform — Filter Trees (CEQL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/activities.md#filter-trees-ceql). |
722	| `node configure` fails with `'<name>' is a FilterBuilder parameter — pass a structured filter tree under --detail.filter` | Same root cause — raw string under `queryParameters` for a FilterBuilder param | Move the value into `--detail.filter` as a structured tree. The CLI catches this at configure time so it never reaches Studio Web. |
723	| Data Service query returns every record (or faults with malformed CEQL ending in `AND`) though a filter tree was configured; `node configure` reported Success | A filter-tree leaf's field id did not match the entity schema (matching is case-sensitive). The compiler drops unmatched leaves without an error — one bad leaf empties the query string, a bad leaf beside a good one leaves a dangling `AND`. | Compare the tree's field ids against the entity schema — `uip df entities list --output json` for the entity `Id`, then `uip df entities get <entity-id> --output json` for the field names. Re-run `node configure` with the exact ids. See Step 6a. |
724	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request`, IS 400 `"Expected a field name expression but got 'StringValue'"` — `flow validate` passed | Hand-authored CEQL string (e.g. Data Service `queryExpression`) quotes the **field name**: `'accountNumber' = '...'`. CEQL reads a quoted token as a string literal. Only `node configure --detail.filter` builds the expression for you; a string hand-written into the `.flow` JSON reaches IS unchecked. | Field names bare, only values quoted: `` `accountNumber = '${$vars...}'` ``. Or author via `--detail.filter` so the CLI compiles the CEQL. |
725	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request`, IS 400 `"Unsupported value expression 'Column' on field '<field>'"` — `flow validate` passed | Hand-authored CEQL double-quotes the **value**, typically from a concatenation with escaped quotes: `` =js:"accountNumber = \"" + String(v) + "\"" ``. CEQL reads a double-quoted token as a column reference, not a string literal. | Single-quote the value inside the concatenation: `` =js:"accountNumber = '" + String($vars.<node>.output.<field>) + "'" ``. Or author via `--detail.filter`. See [Hand-authored CEQL strings](#hand-authored-ceql-strings). |
726	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request` and the filter uses `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `ge`, `lt`, or `le` | OData aliases in a hand-authored CEQL string. CEQL accepts only symbol operators. | Replace with `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`. See the alias table in [Hand-authored CEQL strings](#hand-authored-ceql-strings). |
727	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues must be an array of [key, value] tuples, not an object map` | Wrote `parameterValues: {key: value}` (object map). Studio Web emits its `Map<string,string\|null>` as `Array.from(entries())` — tuples, not object | Convert to tuples: `[["key", "value"], ...]`. See Step 6c. |
728	| Custom fields fault at runtime with token unresolved | A `{token}` in `objectActions[].apiConfiguration.url` or `body` has no entry in `parameterValues` | Re-read the ObjectAction's `apiConfiguration` placeholders, add the missing tuple to `parameterValues`. CLI does not validate token coverage. |
729	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails has unknown keys: ObjectActionName, ParameterValues` | PascalCase inner keys instead of camelCase | Use `objectActionName` / `parameterValues`. Studio Web emits camelCase; PascalCase is rejected. |
730	| Field rejected at runtime as unknown (e.g. `"unknown field 'fields.labels[*]'"`) after a clean `flow validate` | `[*]` was left in the `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key. `[*]` is an array marker from `requestFields[].name`, not part of the wire key. | Strip `[*]` from the key in your `--detail` payload, pass a `=js:` expression returning the array, and re-run `node configure`. Fields with `[*].` (segments after the `[*]`) are not authorable. See the array-fields table in Step 6b. |
731	| Array field round-trips empty after a clean `flow validate` | Literal JSON array authored for a `[*]` field — validates but does not bind | Author as `=js:` expression returning the array: `"users": "=js:(['U123ABC', 'U456DEF'])"`. See the array-fields table in Step 6b. |
732	
733	### Debug Tips
734	
735	1. **Always check top-level `bindings[]` in the `.flow` file** — connector nodes silently fail if a binding is missing or malformed. Compare against the CLI-emitted `bindings[]` shape documented above (§ Top-level `bindings[]` shape). Do not inspect `bindings_v2.json` as ground truth; it is regenerated from the `.flow` on every debug/pack.
736	2. **Compare inputs against metadataFile** — the full metadata (from `is resources describe`) has every field with types, descriptions, and whether it's required
737	3. **`flow validate` does NOT catch connector-specific issues** — validation only checks JSON schema and graph structure. Missing `inputs.detail` fields, wrong reference IDs, and expired connections are caught only at runtime (`flow debug`)
738	4. **If a connector key doesn't work** — list all connectors: `uip is connectors list --output json`. Keys are often prefixed with `uipath-`
739	5. **Query/path parameters** — some required parameters appear only in the metadataFile `parameters` section, not in `requestFields`. Check both.
740	6. **`node configure` populates bindings automatically** — it appends the two top-level `bindings[]` entries and populates `inputs.detail`. The generated `bindings_v2.json` follows from these at debug/pack time. If you cannot run `node configure` (no live tenant, sandbox forbids it, planning-only request), record the planned binding entries in the sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` per the No-Live-Tenant flow above — do not author `bindings[]` directly on the `.flow` as a substitute, and note that the flow will not pass `flow validate` until a real `node configure` runs.
741

1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 **Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py ` scans every `core.action.script` body and every `=js:` expression for the unsupported constructs listed above, plus the script-node rules (top-level `return` of an object, no `function main()` wrapper, no `console.log`, no `aggregate` variable). None of these are caught by `uip maestro flow validate`. 542 543 --- 544 545 ## Scoping Rules 546 547 ### Node Output Availability 548 549 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 550 551 ### Loop Scope 552 553 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 554 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 555 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 556 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 557 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 558 559 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 560 561 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 562 563 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 564 565 ### Subflow Scope 566 567 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 568 569 --- 570 571 ## Variable Management via CLI 572 573 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 574 575 ### Adding a workflow input variable 576 577 1. Open `.flow` 578 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 579 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 580 581 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 582 583 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 584 585 ```json 586 { 587 "id": "myScript.output", 588 "type": "object", 589 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 590 }, 591 { 592 "id": "myScript.error", 593 "type": "object", 594 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 595 } 596 ``` 597 598 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 599 600 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 601 602 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 603 604 ```json 605 "outputs": { 606 "result": { 607 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 608 } 609 } 610 ``` 611 612 --- 613 614 ## Complete Example 615 616 A flow with input, state, and output variables: 617 618 ```json 619 { 620 "variables": { 621 "globals": [ 622 { 623 "id": "inputItems", 624 "direction": "in", 625 "type": "array", 626 "subType": "object", 627 "defaultValue": [], 628 "description": "Items to process" 629 }, 630 { 631 "id": "processedCount", 632 "direction": "inout", 633 "type": "number", 634 "defaultValue": 0 635 }, 636 { 637 "id": "result", 638 "direction": "out", 639 "type": "object", 640 "description": "Processing summary" 641 } 642 ], 643 "nodes": [ 644 { 645 "id": "transform1.output", 646 "type": "object", 647 "binding": { "nodeId": "transform1", "outputId": "output" } 648 } 649 ], 650 "variableUpdates": { 651 "transform1": [ 652 { 653 "variableId": "processedCount", 654 "expression": "=js:$vars.processedCount + $vars.transform1.output.count" 655 } 656 ] 657 } 658 }, 659 "nodes": [ 660 { 661 "id": "start", 662 "type": "core.trigger.manual", 663 "typeVersion": "1.0", 664 "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" }, 665 "inputs": { 666 "entryPointId": "" 667 }, 668 "outputs": { 669 "output": { 670 "type": "object", 671 "description": "Data passed when the flow is triggered manually.", 672 "source": "null", 673 "var": "output" 674 } 675 } 676 }, 677 { 678 "id": "transform1", 679 "type": "core.action.script", 680 "typeVersion": "1.0", 681 "inputs": { 682 "script": "const items = $vars.inputItems.filter(i => i.active);\nreturn { count: items.length, items: items };" 683 }, 684 "outputs": { 685 "output": { 686 "type": "object", 687 "description": "The return value of the script", 688 "source": "=result.response", 689 "var": "output" 690 }, 691 "error": { 692 "type": "object", 693 "description": "Error information if the script fails", 694 "source": "=Error", 695 "var": "error" 696 } 697 } 698 }, 699 { 700 "id": "end1", 701 "type": "core.control.end", 702 "typeVersion": "1.0", 703 "display": { "label": "End" }, 704 "inputs": {}, 705 "outputs": { 706 "result": { 707 "source": "=js:({ total: $vars.processedCount, data: $vars.transform1.output })" 708 } 709 } 710 } 711 ], 712 "edges": [ 713 { 714 "id": "e1", 715 "sourceNodeId": "start", 716 "sourcePort": "output", 717 "targetNodeId": "transform1", 718 "targetPort": "input" 719 }, 720 { 721 "id": "e2", 722 "sourceNodeId": "transform1", 723 "sourcePort": "success", 724 "targetNodeId": "end1", 725 "targetPort": "input" 726 } 727 ] 728 } 729 ``` 730

1	# Script Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.action.script`
6	
7	## Registry validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.action.script --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input port `input`, output port `success`, required input `script` (string, non-empty). See [Action Node Structure — Registry validation](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#registry-validation) for the shared pattern.
14	
15	## JSON structure
16	
17	Follow the [Action Node Structure — Standard JSON skeleton](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#standard-json-skeleton). The script-specific input is a single `script` string:
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "inputs": {
22	    "script": "const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;\nconst total = items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.amount, 0);\nreturn { total, count: items.length };"
23	  }
24	}
25	```
26	
27	## Adding and editing
28	
29	See [Action Node Structure — Adding and editing procedures](../../../../shared/action-nodes.md#adding-and-editing-procedures). The script node uses the standard input port `input` and output port `success`; no plugin-specific wiring.
30	
31	## Script rules
32	
33	1. **Top-level body — no `function main()` wrapper.** Node runs the `script` text directly (as a function body); a wrapper is never called → `output` null. Read workflow variables via `$vars.<variableId>` and upstream node outputs via `$vars.<nodeId>.output`; end with top-level `return {…}`. Not a coded Function: no `main`, no injected args.
34	   - Correct: `const n = $vars.ixp1.output.field; return { n };`
35	   - Wrong: `function main({ ixp1 }) { … }`
36	2. **Must `return` an object** — `return { key: value }`, not a bare scalar. The return value becomes `$vars.<nodeId>.output`.
37	3. **`$vars` is a global** — use it directly: `return { upper: $vars.customerName.toUpperCase() }`
38	4. **JavaScript ES2020 (Jint engine)** — see [variables-and-expressions.md](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md) for supported features and Jint constraints.
39	5. **No `console.log`** — `console` is not available. Use `return { debug: value }` to inspect values.
40	6. **No external calls** — use the HTTP node or a connector node for API calls.
41	7. **30-second timeout** — long-running computations will be killed.
42	8. **Never name a variable `aggregate`** — reserved host global. On any `Identifier 'X' has already been declared`, rename `X`.
43	
44	**Script:** `python3 scripts/lint_jint.py <ProjectName>.flow` checks rules 1, 2, 5, 6 and 8 above (plus the wider unsupported-construct list) across every script node and `=js:` expression in the file. The 30-second timeout is a runtime property and is not statically checkable.
45	
46	## Common patterns
47	
48	### Transform and return
49	
50	```javascript
51	const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items;
52	const filtered = items.filter(i => i.status === "active");
53	return { items: filtered, count: filtered.length };
54	```
55	
56	### Build a payload for a downstream node
57	
58	```javascript
59	return {
60	  subject: `Order ${$vars.orderId} - Confirmation`,
61	  body: `Your order of ${$vars.orderTotal} has been processed.`,
62	  recipient: $vars.customerEmail
63	};
64	```
65	
66	### Error check from upstream
67	
68	```javascript
69	const error = $vars.httpCall.error;
70	if (error) {
71	  return { hasError: true, message: error.message };
72	}
73	return { hasError: false, data: $vars.httpCall.output.body };
74	```
75	
76	### Reading a file-typed variable
77	
78	A `file` variable (bound via `uip maestro flow debug --attachment <id>=<path>`) hydrates as an **object**, not a string. Read the uploaded file's name from `.FullName`:
79	
80	```javascript
81	const doc = $vars.start.output.inputDoc; // file variable → object
82	return { fileName: doc.FullName };        // .FullName, not .name/.fileName
83	```
84	
85	Property access is **case-sensitive** — these casings resolve: `.FullName`, `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.MimeType`, `.Metadata.size` (nested, lowercase `size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do not exist. See [variables-and-expressions.md — Runtime shape of a `file` variable](../../../../shared/variables-and-expressions.md#file-input).
86	
87	## Debug
88	
89	| Error | Cause | Fix |
90	| --- | --- | --- |
91	| Script did not return a value | Missing `return` statement | Add `return { ... }` |
92	| `output` is `null` but script has a `return` | `return` is inside an uncalled `function main(){}` wrapper | Remove wrapper; code + `return` at top level (rule 1) |
93	| Return value is not an object | Returned a scalar (`return 42`) | Wrap in object: `return { value: 42 }` |
94	| `$vars.nodeId` is undefined | Upstream node not connected or wrong ID | Check edges and node IDs |
95	| Timeout after 30s | Script too expensive | Simplify logic or split into multiple scripts |
96	| `console is not defined` | Used `console.log()` | Remove — use `return { debug: val }` instead |
97	| `fetch is not defined` | Tried to make HTTP call | Use an HTTP node or connector node instead |
98	| `[300501] Error invoking script task` with `Unexpected token` | Malformed JavaScript — `flow validate` does not parse script bodies, so syntax errors surface only at runtime. Common slip: one missing `)` in chained `(((a \|\| {}).b \|\| {}).c \|\| [])` guards | Balance parentheses; check with `node -e "new Function(<script>)"` before validate |
99	| `Identifier 'X' has already been declared` | `X` collides with a runtime-injected global (known: `aggregate`) | Rename `X` (e.g. `agg`) |
100

commands.result_summary:
65:## Filter Trees (CEQL)
66-
67:Some IS activities — most notably **List All Records** and other list/query operations — accept a server-side filter expressed in **CEQL** (Connector Expression Query Language). As with trigger filters (which compile to JMESPath), CEQL filters are authored as a **structured filter tree** and the CLI compiles them to a CEQL string. Authoring as a tree keeps the CLI and Studio Web in lockstep so the activity round-trips cleanly when re-opened in SW.
68-
69-### Contract — three signals from IS metadata
70-
71-The CLI reads the live IS metadata response and uses three signals to wire the filter:
72-
73:1. **The activity supports CEQL** when one of its `parameters` declares `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. That parameter's `name` is the connector-specific key the compiled CEQL string is sent under — most commonly `where`, but **not always** (e.g. Salesforce uses `q`). Activities with no such parameter do not support server-side filtering — pass no `filter` and filter downstream.
74-2. **A field is filterable** when its IS metadata entry has `searchable: true`. Type alone does not gate it — the connector flags fields explicitly. Fields without `searchable: true` are rejected by the CLI even if they look like primitives.
75:3. **Permitted operators** for the field are listed under `searchableOperators`. **Connector-side identifier** for the field in CEQL is `searchableNames[0]` when present (some connectors expose a friendly `name` but require a different identifier in the query string).
76-
77-### What the CLI persists from a single `filter` input
78-
79:- **Runtime side** — the compiled CEQL string lands at `inputs.detail.queryParameters.<filterParamName>` where `<filterParamName>` is the FilterBuilder parameter's name from the IS metadata (often `where`).
80:- **Design-time side** — the structured tree is embedded under `inputs.detail.configuration`'s `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>`. Studio Web reads this on open to re-render the filter widget; without it the filter UI shows up empty even though the runtime call still works.
81-
82-Pass `filter` (the structured tree) and the CLI emits both halves in lockstep. Passing both `filter` and `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` is rejected at validation time — single source of truth.
83-
84-### Tree shape
85-
86:Identical to the trigger filter tree — the same `FilterTree` / `Filter` / `WorkflowValue` types are used; only the compiler output (CEQL vs JMESPath) differs.
87-
88-```jsonc
89-{
90-  "groupOperator": 0,             // 0 = And, 1 = Or — combines sibling filters/groups
91-  "index": 0,                     // ordering index within parent (root is 0)
92-  "filters": [                    // leaf conditions at this level
93-    {
94-      "id": "<fieldName>",        // resource field name from `is resources describe`
95-      "operator": "<Operator>",   // PascalCase, see operator table below
96-      "value": {
97-        "value": <typed value>,   // string / number / boolean / ISO-8601 date-time / array
98-        "rawString": "\"...\"",   // verbatim user-entered text (with quotes for strings)
99-        "isLiteral": true         // literals only — expression values are not yet supported
100-      }
101-    }
102-  ],
103-  "groups": []                    // optional: nested subgroups (same shape as root)
104-}
105-```
106-
107-A no-op filter — used when the user wants to list all records without restriction — is `null` or `{"groupOperator": null, "index": 0, "filters": []}`. Prefer **omitting** the `filter` field entirely.
108-
109:### Compiled CEQL output
110-
111-The CLI compiles each leaf to `<field> <op> <value>` (or `<field> <function>` for null checks) and joins siblings with the group operator. String values are wrapped in single quotes; booleans, numerics, and enums are passed bare.
112-
113:| Operator | CEQL token | Notes |
114-|---|---|---|
115-| `Equals` | `=` | |
116-| `NotEquals` | `!=` | |
117-| `LessThan` / `LessThanOrEqual` / `GreaterThan` / `GreaterThanOrEqual` | `<` / `<=` / `>` / `>=` | Numeric / date-time |
118-| `Contains` / `NotContains` | `Contains` / `Not Contains` | Substring (string) |
119-| `StartsWith` / `NotStartsWith` / `EndsWith` / `NotEndsWith` | `Starts With` / `Not Starts With` / `Ends With` / `Not Ends With` | String |
120-| `Like` / `NotLike` | `Like` / `Not Like` | Pattern match (connector-specific) |
121-| `In` / `NotIn` | `In` / `Not In` | Membership — `value.value` is a list; rendered as `(v1, v2, …)` |
122-| `IsNull` / `IsNotNull` | `Is Null` / `Is Not Null` | No `value` needed |
123-| `Is` / `IsNot` | `=` against literal `true` / `false` | Boolean shortcut |
124-
125-Logical operators between siblings:
126-
127:| `groupOperator` | CEQL token |
128-|---|---|
129-| `0` (And) | ` AND ` |
130-| `1` (Or) | ` OR ` |
131-
132-### Examples
133-
134-**Active accounts only:**
135-
136-```json
137-{
138-  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
139-  "filters": [
140-    { "id": "Status", "operator": "Equals",
141-      "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }
142-  ]
143-}
144-```
145:→ CEQL: `Status = 'Active'`
146-
147-**Score ≥ 80 AND Region in (EMEA, APAC):**
148-
149-```json
150-{
151-  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
152-  "filters": [
153-    { "id": "Score", "operator": "GreaterThanOrEqual",
154-      "value": { "value": 80, "rawString": "80", "isLiteral": true } },
155-    { "id": "Region", "operator": "In",
156-      "value": { "value": ["EMEA", "APAC"], "rawString": "[\"EMEA\",\"APAC\"]", "isLiteral": true } }
157-  ]
158-}
159-```
160:→ CEQL: `Score >= 80 AND Region In ('EMEA', 'APAC')`
161-
162-**Subject contains "urgent" AND (owner = me OR owner is null):**
163-
164-```json
165-{
166-  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
167-  "filters": [
168-    { "id": "Subject", "operator": "Contains",
169-      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
170-  ],
171-  "groups": [
172-    {
173-      "groupOperator": 1, "index": 1,
174-      "filters": [
175-        { "id": "OwnerId", "operator": "Equals",
176-          "value": { "value": "${me.id}", "rawString": "\"${me.id}\"", "isLiteral": false } },
177-        { "id": "OwnerId", "operator": "IsNull" }
178-      ]
179-    }
180-  ]
181-}
182-```
183:→ CEQL: `Subject Contains 'urgent' AND (OwnerId = ${me.id} OR OwnerId Is Null)`. Non-literal values (`isLiteral: false`) are emitted as `${expression}` placeholders for runtime resolution.
184-
185:### How to build a CEQL filter tree
186-
187-1. Run `uip is resources describe "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id "<id>" --operation List` to read the resource's metadata.
188:2. **Confirm CEQL is supported** for this operation: at least one entry under `parameters` must carry `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. If none does, the activity does not support server-side filtering — omit `filter` and filter downstream (e.g. with a Script node).
189-3. **Pick filterable fields** from `fields[]` where `searchable: true`. Other fields will be rejected by the CLI at configure time even if they look like primitives.
190-4. For each leaf, pick an operator from the field's `searchableOperators` list (when present). Date-time fields take ISO-8601 strings; enums take the literal enum value.
191:5. Use the field's `name` as the leaf `id`. The CLI rewrites it to `searchableNames[0]` when emitting CEQL if the connector declares one — you don't need to use the alias yourself.
192-6. Build one leaf per condition; place multiple conditions under the same `groupOperator` (0 for AND, 1 for OR). Use nested `groups` for mixed AND/OR.
193-7. Wrap values in a `WorkflowValue` object with `value`, `rawString`, `isLiteral`. Strings, numbers, booleans, dates, and arrays are all valid `value` types; only `isLiteral: true` is currently supported by activity-side compilation.
194-
195-### What NOT to generate
196-
197-| Invalid input | Why it fails | Valid replacement |
198-|---|---|---|
199:| `"filter": "Status = 'Active'"` | Bare CEQL string — `filter` must be an object. | Structured tree with `filters: [...]`. |
200:| `"filterExpression": "..."` | That field is reserved for the trigger (JMESPath) path. | Use `filter` (CEQL tree) for activities. |
201-| `{ "operator": "equals", ... }` | Operator is case-sensitive. | `"operator": "Equals"` |
202-| `{ "value": "Active" }` on a leaf | Bare string — must be wrapped in the `WorkflowValue` object. | `{ "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }` |
203-| `{ "id": "fields.Status", ... }` | `fields.` prefix — use the bare field name from `is resources describe`. | `{ "id": "Status", ... }` |
204-| `{ "id": "<field without searchable: true>", ... }` | The CLI checks `searchable` on the IS metadata entry; non-searchable fields are rejected even if their type looks filterable. | Pick a field where `searchable: true`. |
205-| `"queryParameters": { "where": "..." }` alongside `filter` | Hardcoding `where` assumes that's the FilterBuilder param name — it isn't always (Salesforce uses `q`, etc.). | Pass `filter` only; the CLI discovers the right param name from `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. |
206-| `In` operator with a single value not in a list | `In` expects an array `value`. | Use `Equals`, or pass `value: ["one"]`. |
207-
208-## Custom Fields (`objectActions[ActionType=Api]`)
209-
210-Connectors with extensible/custom fields (Jira project+issuetype → custom Jira fields, Mailchimp list_id → audience merge fields, Salesforce custom objects) expose `Api`-type entries under `objectActions[]`. Each entry's `apiConfiguration.url`/`body` carries `{token}` placeholders naming the parent fields. The runtime replays the ObjectAction with cached parent values to fetch the connector-specific custom-field schema.
211-
212-**For Maestro flows**, this lives on the activity node as `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails`. Authoring contract → [uipath-maestro-flow connector/impl.md Step 6c](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md).
213-
214-Shape:
215-
216-```json
217-"customFieldsRequestDetails": {
218-  "objectActionName": "GenerateSchema",
219-  "parameterValues": [["fields_sub_project_sub_key", "ENGCE"], ...]
220-}
221-```
222-
223-camelCase inner keys, `parameterValues` as `[key, value]` tuples (Studio Web emits `Map<string,string|null>` via `Array.from(entries())`). Object-map form rejected by the CLI.

1	# UiPath Flow File Format
2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (generated scaffold)](#project-structure-generated-scaffold)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
